items.title: EU oil: Vår pays USD 4.4bn for ConocoPhillips Norway, 23 Nov 2026
items.summary: Sector Notes: EU Oil · Mon 23 Nov · Vår pays USD 4.4bn for ConocoPhillips Norway
items.text: Sector Notes: EU Oil · Mon 23 Nov · Vår pays USD 4.4bn for ConocoPhillips Norway Sector Notes: EU oil and gas Mon 23 Nov 2026 · news since Fri 20 Nov 09:30 (Zurich) Oil price Brent 91.36 1d −1.3% 1m −18.2% 1y +47.3% 52-WK RANGE BZF27.​NYM · 1 month Brent for January delivery was at USD 91.36 a barrel, down 1.3% on Friday's close and down 1.2% on a week ago (USD 92.44 on Mon 16 Nov). A selloff in equities and the expected supply surplus are weighing on crude ahead of the ministerial meeting of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies (OPEC+) on Sunday 29 November, which is due to set 2027 quotas. Reports of tankers hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz limit the fall. Vår Energi has agreed to buy ConocoPhillips' Norway business, the main item in this note. Brokers estimate the deal implies a long-term oil price of about USD 75 to 85, below today's level. Vår Energi (VAR.​OL, NOK 44.96/sh, MC EUR 10.5bn; EV EUR 13.5bn) Acquires ConocoPhillips (COP, USD 136.12/sh, MC EUR 147bn; EV EUR 159bn)'s Norwegian upstream assets for USD 4.4bn. VAR 44.96 1d −2.7% 1m −23.7% 1y +42.3% Mkt cap 112bn EV 145bn 52-WK RANGE VAR.​OL · 1 month ENI 23.92 1d −1.0% 1m −13.5% 1y +52.3% Mkt cap 67.9bn EV 88.1bn 52-WK RANGE ENI.​MI · 1 month Including operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area, plus related infrastructure in Norway and the UK Teesside terminal (a 40.25% stake and operatorship, per ConocoPhillips ). The enterprise value is USD 4.425 billion from a 1 January 2026 economic date (the date from which the buyer takes the cash flow). Cash at completion, expected around the end of the first quarter of 2027 subject to Norwegian Ministry of Energy approval, is put at about USD 2.5 billion, net of cash flow earned by the business since the economic date and other adjustments. Including the previously announced BlueNord combination, pro-forma 2026 production rises to about 550 thousand barrels of oil equivalent (boe) a day (kboepd) and reserves and resources to about 2.9 billion boe. The long-term target is now to hold output above 500 kboepd into the mid-2030s, synergies are put at USD 700 million to 1 billion, and fourth-quarter dividend guidance rises to USD 450 million. It is funded from USD 7.5 billion of liquidity, with a gas hedge on most of the added volumes (details below). Eni stays majority owner. The deal puts Ekofisk, the shelf's oldest hub, with a growth-focused independent backed by Eni, and is Vår's third deal since June, after Pandion and the BlueNord combination; the possible equity raise is the near-term overhang for the shares. The Vår deal in 90 seconds USD 4.4bn (enterprise value) | USD 10.7 per 2P boe | about 0.7x leverage pro forma (our calc) Vår becomes operator of Ekofisk, Norway's oldest oil hub, and lifts its long-term output goal to above 500 kboepd, paying about USD 2.5 billion in cash at completion. On a reserve multiple the price is only slightly below Vår's own rating; the open questions are a rising unit cost, an undisclosed decommissioning bill and three deals to absorb since June. What Vår is buying • Interests in 13 producing fields on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), 5 of them operated: the Greater Ekofisk Area (Ekofisk, Eldfisk, Embla, Tor, Tommeliten), plus Troll, Heidrun, Alvheim, Oseberg, Visund, Aasta Hansteen, Grane and Breidablikk. • Output of about 115 kboepd net in the first nine months of 2026, about half gas; ConocoPhillips puts 2025 at about 120 kboepd. • Reserves: 414 million boe (mmboe) of net proved plus probable (2P) reserves plus 101 mmboe of contingent (2C) resources at end-2025. ConocoPhillips reports 221 mmboe of proved reserves. About 75% of the 2P sits in fields where Vår is already a partner. • Infrastructure: 35.05% of the Norpipe oil line and a 40.25% stake in, and operatorship of, the Teesside terminal in the UK. Price and metrics • Price bridge: EV USD 4.425 billion from 1 January 2026, less about USD 1.9 billion of cash flow earned since then and other adjustments, gives about USD 2.5 billion of cash at completion; add the business's 2026 tax bill of about USD 1.4 billion, paid in the first half of 2027, and the total is about USD 3.9 billion (ConocoPhillips' figure). • Multiples: on the USD 4.425 billion EV, USD 10.7 per 2P boe (Vår) and about USD 38,500 per flowing boe a day (our calc); the tables use EV throughout. On the USD 3.9 billion total it is USD 9.4 per 2P boe (our calc), and on the completion cash against reserves after this year's output about USD 7 (Vår). The 2C resources and the USD 0.7 billion to 1 billion of synergies come on top. Past deals Date Deal (value, USD) EV per 2P boe EV per boe/d Nov 2026 Vår Energi buys ConocoPhillips Norway EV 4.4bn 10.7 38,500 Jul 2026 Vår Energi and BlueNord combination (Danish shelf) EV ~2.3bn* 13.3 51,100 Jun 2026 Vår Energi buys Pandion's NCS portfolio 110m cash n.d. n.d. Mar 2025 DNO buys Sval Energi (from HitecVision) EV 1.6bn 11.3 25,000 Dec 2023 Harbour buys Wintershall Dea (about half Norway) EV 11.2bn c.10 c.35,000 Jun 2023 Vår Energi buys Neptune Norway EV 2.3bn 8.6 34,000 Dec 2021 Aker BP buys Lundin Energy oil and gas 13.9bn** 20.7 73,200 Our calc unless stated: EV over 2P reserves at the last year-end before the deal, and over output at the time. *BlueNord EV per RBC (secondary). **Aker BP and Lundin: reported deal value (cash plus shares, Reuters, secondary); Lundin's net debt is not added, so the true EV multiples were higher. n.d. = not disclosed. Dates are announcements. Deals struck at different oil prices. Listed peers today Company EV (USD bn) EV per 2P boe EV per boe/d Aker BP 27.1 17.7 72,300 Vår Energi 14.6 11.3 39,600 DNO 2.3 5.9 16,200 OKEA 0.3 4.2 10,800 BlueNord 2.4 14.0 55,300 Equinor (reference) 100.0 19.3 46,200 Deal: ConocoPhillips Norway 4.4 10.7 38,500 Market caps today (Yahoo Finance), USD/NOK 9.7375; plus net interest-bearing debt at 30 Sep 2026 (Aker BP and Equinor include leases; OKEA is net cash); 2P at end-2025; output third quarter 2026. DNO is about half Kurdistan and BlueNord is Danish; Equinor uses proved (1P) reserves. Pandion is unlisted (its last assets went to Vår, closing in September), so it is left out. The deal, at USD 10.7 per 2P boe, sits about 5% below Vår (11.3) and about 40% below Aker BP (17.7), and well below Equinor (19.3). • Per 2P barrel it is in line with Neptune (Jun 2023), Sval (Mar 2025) and Wintershall Dea (Dec 2023), though richer per flowing barrel, and roughly half what Aker BP paid for Lundin (Dec 2021), which bought into Johan Sverdrup's long plateau. • Smaller producers such as OKEA and DNO trade at a fraction of these deal prices, which reflects size, reserve life and, for DNO, Kurdistan risk. Funding, balance sheet, dividend • Paid from USD 7.5 billion of available liquidity at 30 September plus cash in the acquired company at closing; its slides say no additional interest-bearing debt is incurred. • Leverage, net interest-bearing debt (NIBD) to EBITDAX (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and exploration), was 0.3x at end-September: NIBD USD 3.1 billion against USD 10.3 billion of rolling 12-month EBITDAX (Q3 report). Vår gives no pro-forma figure; adding the USD 2.5 billion completion cash and USD 1.4 billion tax gives about 0.7x on Vår's own EBITDAX (our calc), before the acquired business's earnings (not disclosed) and BlueNord's debt. The ceiling is 1.3x. • Gas hedge: a floor (downside protection, upside kept) of about USD 110 per boe on about 80% of the added gas volumes, for 2027 through the first quarter of 2028, roughly USD 19 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) at 5.8 mmBtu per boe (our conversion). That is well above the USD 12 to 13 gas ABG Sundal Collier says the price implies. No oil hedge was announced. • Equity: Vår will assess raising up to 10% under its board authorisation, subject to markets, and says the deal adds to earnings, cash flow and dividend capacity per share with or without it. A raise would dilute existing holders, including majority owner Eni, unless they take up their share; Vår says Eni will remain the majority shareholder. • Dividend: fourth-quarter 2026 guidance rises to USD 450 million from USD 400 million; the policy of 25% to 30% of cash flow from operations after tax is unchanged. Why do it • Scale: about 550 kboepd pro forma for 2026 including BlueNord, and a long-term goal raised to above 500 kboepd into the mid-2030s (about 450 before). Reserves and resources (2P plus 2C) of about 2.9 billion boe cover about 14 years of 2026 output (Vår); 2P alone, about 1.9 billion boe, covers about 9.5 years (our calc). • Ekofisk: the first commercial NCS find, with 4.3 billion boe produced (more than four times the first estimate) out of about 10 billion in place. Vår wants to repeat what it did at Balder and Goliat: extend field life and lift recovery. • Synergies of USD 0.7 billion to 1 billion, net present value (NPV) after tax at 8%: supply chain, transport, gas sales and overheads. • Eni remains the majority owner, which backs the balance sheet and the growth plan. Risks • A mature hub: Vår takes on the business's decommissioning liabilities with the shares. It says near-term abandonment costs are limited, but neither company discloses the size of the liability. • Costs: pro-forma unit operating cost of about USD 13 per boe for 2027 to 2029, against the USD 10 to 11 guided in July with the BlueNord combination, a figure that already included BlueNord. The slides don't explain the rise. RBC puts BlueNord's own unit cost at USD 25.7 per boe in 2026 year to date (secondary), a current reading rather than the 2027 to 2029 guide. • Three deals to absorb: Pandion (closed 30 September), BlueNord around the end of 2026 and ConocoPhillips around the end of March 2027, including a large operated hub and its staff. • Prices: the mix stays about 65% oil and 35% gas, and only the added gas is hedged. • Approvals: the Norwegian Ministry of Energy, other regulators, licence partners. What the brokers say • ABG Sundal Collier (Sell rating) likes the deal: it puts the price at about USD 9 per 2P boe at end-2026, implying oil at USD 75 to 80 and gas at USD 12 to 13 per mmBtu, 15% to 20% below how the market values Vår on that end-2026 figure (our table, on the headline USD 10.7, is about 5% below Vår's USD 11.3). • Arctic Securities (Hold rating) sees the price at the top of its range, implying long-term oil of about USD 85: full value before synergies and broadly neutral. SEB (Sell rating) is puzzled by Vår's eagerness to buy for cash this high in the cycle. All three flag the possible equity raise. What it means for the sector • NCS consolidation keeps going (announcement dates): Aker BP and Lundin (Dec 2021), Vår and Neptune (Jun 2023), Harbour and Wintershall Dea (Dec 2023), DNO and Sval (Mar 2025), Vår and Pandion (Jun 2026) and now ConocoPhillips. Vår's BlueNord combination (Jul 2026) takes the same play to the Danish shelf. • US majors keep leaving: ExxonMobil sold its Norwegian fields to Vår in 2019, and ConocoPhillips now exits after more than five decades, putting the proceeds towards 2027 share buybacks. • Output is concentrating in Equinor, Aker BP and Vår, while smaller listed producers trade far below what buyers pay for barrels. What to watch • Around the end of 2026: BlueNord combination completes. • 26 January 2027: Vår's fourth-quarter trading update. 9 February 2027: fourth-quarter results and capital markets update. • No date set: the possible equity raise of up to 10%, market permitting. • First half of 2027: the 2026 tax payment of about USD 1.4 billion. Around end-March 2027: completion, after Ministry of Energy approval. The Norwegian Offshore Directorate (Sodir) (not listed) published preliminary October production figures . Sodir · unlisted Average output was 2,030,000 barrels a day of oil, natural gas liquids (NGL) and condensate, up from 1,866,000 in September (an 8.8% month-on-month rise). That was 1.4% above Sodir's October forecast; oil alone was 5.9% above forecast. Liquids were 3.4% below October 2025 (published Friday). Output running ahead of forecast (oil 4.1% above Sodir's forecast so far this year) supports the cash flow of Norwegian producers, including the barrels Vår is buying. TotalEnergies (TTE.​PA, EUR 78.25/sh, MC EUR 171bn; EV EUR 198bn) will acquire interests from Continental Resources (not listed). TTE 78.25 1d +0.1% 1m −6.2% 1y +40.0% Mkt cap 171bn EV 198bn 52-WK RANGE TTE.​PA · 1 month The interests are expected to add about 150 million cubic feet a day (around 26 kboe/d) of US net gas production by 2032, lifting its US net gas output to about 850 million cubic feet a day (over 140 kboe/d) from 2032; it exported 19 million tonnes of US liquefied natural gas (LNG) in 2025, 14 million of them to Europe. The added volumes are TotalEnergies' net interest from Continental Resources and, at about 150 million cubic feet a day by 2032, a modest lift relative to the 19 million tonnes of US LNG it exported in 2025, 14 million of them to Europe. Eco Atlantic (ECO.​L, GBp 39.30/sh, MC EUR 173m; EV EUR 163m) published an operator update for Falklands licence PL001 after buying JHI Associates (not listed); operator Navitas (NVPT.​TA, ILA 10,970/sh, MC EUR 3.70bn; EV EUR 5.35bn) plans Sea Lion development drilling from March 2027. ECO 39.30 1d +3.4% 1m +0.8% 1y +442.1% Mkt cap £145m EV £136m 52-WK RANGE ECO.​L · 1 month NVPT 10,970 1d −2.1% 1m −9.0% 1y −4.3% Mkt cap 13.5bn ILS EV 19.6bn ILS 52-WK RANGE NVPT.​TA · 1 month Eco holds 35% after the JHI purchase (announced 17 November). First oil is expected in mid-2028. Navitas is considering a multi-target PL001 exploration well in 2027 with gross best-estimate prospective resources of about 640 million boe (about 225 million net to Eco). Navitas carries Eco's share of the first USD 40 million through a loan capped at USD 14 million net, repaid from 85% of Eco's future PL001 free cash flow; the well's timing is not confirmed. Sources: Vår Energi and ConocoPhillips releases, ABG, Arctic and SEB broker notes, Sodir. Prices: Yahoo Finance. Bubble = 1-day change; 1m = one-month change; 1y = one-year change; candles = last 22 sessions; bar = 52-week range, tick = now. Lead-line market cap and EV are in euro at Yahoo Finance FX. Company figures from releases and filings; “our calc” marks our own. Brent: January 2027 futures contract via Yahoo Finance. Deal and peer figures from company releases and reports; broker views from this morning's notes; secondary figures marked. Commentary, not investment advice.

items.title: Data centre infrastructure: the build-out, the debt and the rate squeeze
items.summary: Special report, Monday 23 November 2026. What is being built, how it is now financed, what 5% long rates do to it, three scenarios with dated signposts, and who is exposed. Views only, not investment advice.
items.text: Data centre infrastructure: the build-out, the debt and the rate squeeze Skip to content Back to EMMI Light Special report Data centre infrastructure: the build-out, the debt and the rate squeeze Special report, Monday 23 November 2026. What is being built, how it is now financed, what 5% long rates do to it, three scenarios with dated signposts, and who is exposed. Views only, not investment advice. Edition date Monday 23 November 2026 Kind Special report Topics data centres capex credit rates power neoclouds Source Public filings, central bank material and press reports, accessed 22-23 November 2026. Publication Published on this site from the Markdown report in the analysis store. This page is the site copy. Delivery Email not sent. This report is on the site only. Putting this edition on the site did not send an email. Companies in this report Amazon Alphabet Microsoft Meta Oracle CoreWeave Nebius IREN Nvidia AMD Broadcom Micron Constellation Energy GE Vernova Vertiv Equinix Digital Realty Blue Owl Capital Brookfield Fortum Siemens Energy Schneider Electric ABB Munters Hexatronic NKT Contents Executive summary 1. Where the build-out stands Neoclouds: fast growth, expensive money The big campuses Power is the binding constraint 2. The debt: who is lending, and how How the off-balance-sheet chain works Credit markets are already pricing it 3. Rates: the squeeze 4. Where it is headed Base case: slower and dearer, not a bust Bull case: revenue catches up Bear case: rates plus a revenue miss Signposts and dates What history adds this time 5. Who is exposed Data gaps Sources Executive summary The build-out has not slowed yet. The four largest United States (US) cloud companies (the hyperscalers) guide to about $730bn of capital spending (capex) in 2026 at the midpoints (our sum), and all say 2027 will be higher. None has given a 2027 number. 1 3 5 It is now debt-funded. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft sold $249.4bn of bonds in 2026 to 4 November, three times 2025. Bonds paid for about 43 cents of every capex dollar over the past year. 12 The bigger pile is off the balance sheet. The Federal Reserve (Fed) counts more than $3trn of signed-but-unstarted leases, take-or-pay contracts and guarantees at seven AI firms, against on-balance-sheet debt heading past $800bn. 14 Rates have turned against it. The US 10-year yield closed at 5.046% on 19 November, and markets price a near-certain Fed hike on 8-9 December. Borrowers at the edge pay 7% to 16%. 26 16 25 Credit is separating the strong from the weak. Oracle's five-year credit default swaps (CDS) went from 37.5 basis points (bp) in June 2025 to 305bp on 5 November 2026; CoreWeave's 2032 bonds yield over 16%. Alphabet and Meta still borrow, but pay double the spread of April. 16 25 13 Our base case is a slower, more expensive build-out, not a bust: capex growth peaks in 2027, weaker developers and neoclouds consolidate, and power and grid owners keep their pricing power. The bear case needs an AI revenue miss on top of higher rates. Bottom line The assets that last are power, grid connections and buildings; the layers that break are short-lived chips financed with floating-rate, high-yield or vehicle debt. In a 5% world, the investor question shifts from who builds the most to who can carry the debt until the revenue arrives. This report builds on our 31 October piece on debt-funded booms ("History rhymes"). That piece set out the historical pattern; this one tracks what has changed since, with the November credit and rate shock, and what to watch next. 1. Where the build-out stands 2026 capex guidance · $bn at the midpoint Amazon $220bn Alphabet $195-205bn Microsoft $170bn Meta $135-145bn CoreWeave $37-39bn Nebius $27bn 2026 capex guidance, latest as of each company's October or November results. Ranges plotted at the midpoint. Microsoft is calendar 2026; Oracle gives no calendar figure. 1 2 3 6 47 Amazon kept 2026 cash capex at about $220bn on 29 October and said 2027 will be "meaningfully more". Third-quarter (Q3) capex was $77.3bn, and trailing free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4bn. 3 4 Microsoft cut calendar 2026 to about $170bn from $175bn on 28 October, because third-party capacity was delayed, and expects spending to accelerate in the first half of 2027. About three quarters of Q3 capex went on short-lived chips. 2 1 Alphabet held $195-205bn and said 2027 will "increase significantly"; it reported negative free cash flow of more than $9bn for Q3. Meta raised its floor to $135-145bn and gives 2027 on its fourth-quarter call. 1 5 Oracle gives no dollar figure for fiscal 2027; it says capex peaks in fiscal 2027 and 2028. Its trailing 12-month capex was $75.7bn against $71.8bn of revenue. 19 16 Forecasters: Standard and Poor's put 2027 hyperscaler capex above $1.3trn (15 October); Moody's puts the five largest plus CoreWeave near $1trn (27 October). 15 24 Neoclouds: fast growth, expensive money CoreWeave Nebius Q3 2026 revenue $3.66bn $0.98bn 2026 capex guide $37-39bn about $27bn 2027 capex guide not given $40-45bn Backlog or contracted $132.5bn backlog over $40bn with Microsoft, Meta and similar Total debt (30 Sep) about $46.9bn not stated in letter Debt due in 2027 $10.97bn not found Neoclouds rent graphics processing units (GPUs) to AI labs and hyperscalers. CoreWeave's Q3 net interest expense of $846m was about 2.2 times its adjusted operating income of $379m (our calc), and it guides fourth-quarter interest to $1.05-1.15bn. It says it will issue no more unsecured parent debt through 2027 at current yields, and will lean on contract-backed delayed-draw term loans (DDTLs), customer prepayments of about $9bn in the next three months, and vendor financing. 6 7 8 Nebius raised 2026 capex but cut revenue to the low end of $3.0-3.4bn because capacity slipped. It expects prepayments and asset-backed loans to fund 75-85% of 2027 capex, and closed a $775m facility at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 2.50% in July. 9 47 The big campuses Meta Hyperion (Louisiana): about $27bn joint venture, 80% Blue Owl funds, 20% Meta, funded with $27.3bn of bonds. 10 11 Oracle and OpenAI (Texas): Abilene "nearly complete"; Shackelford, the next gigawatt (GW) campus, fully permitted; Oracle says the contract is fully funded (20 November). 18 SB Energy PORTS-Pike (Ohio): about 4.25GW across nine buildings, leased to OpenAI for 20 years, with Nvidia credit support capped at $105bn. 20 14 Brookfield: plans a $27bn AI data centre at a UK power station (reported 6 November). 39 Nordics: atNorth sold for $4bn to Canada Pension Plan Investments and Equinix. 37 Power is the binding constraint Chips are no longer the scarcest input; powered buildings are. Nvidia's new guarantees exist precisely because "powered shells are now the bottleneck", in one analyst's words. 20 Grid: the PJM Interconnection (PJM), the largest US grid operator, cleared its 2027/2028 capacity auction at the $333.44 per megawatt (MW) per day cap and fell 6,517MW short of its reliability target. About 5,100MW of the 5,250MW load increase was data centres. 32 Gas turbines: GE Vernova had 122GW of gas backlog and slot reservations at Q3, effectively booked through 2029. Siemens Energy's gas turbine backlog is 65GW; data centres are about €15bn, under 10% of its €164bn total backlog. 33 34 Nuclear: deals are uprates of existing reactors, not new builds. Google and Constellation agreed 890MW of uprates (first in 2028); Amazon signed a 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA) at Calvert Cliffs including a 190MW uprate due 2030-2032. 35 36 Politics: on 3 November voters backed restrictions in nearly all of 41 data centre ballot measures across 10 states; Texas's governor-elect pledged a moratorium. Between January 2024 and May 2026, at least 46 projects with more than $170bn of planned investment were blocked or stalled. 39 Nordic market Large-load power price, first half 2026 Policy signal Norway €0.071 per kWh cheapest of the three Finland €0.079 per kWh nearly 5GW with signed grid agreements (Aug); data centre power tax raised Sweden €0.090 per kWh highest of the three Denmark not found most large data centres put in a lower grid-priority queue Prices per kilowatt-hour (kWh), excluding value added tax, for a 70-150 gigawatt-hour (GWh) a year load; sources say prices rose sharply year on year. The Nordic pitch of cheap clean power and cool air still holds, but grid access and tax, not tariffs, now decide which projects proceed. 37 38 2. The debt: who is lending, and how US-registered hyperscaler bond issuance · $bn 2025 2026 to 4 Nov Amazon 15.0 94.6 Alphabet 37.7 79.7 Meta 30.0 50.1 Microsoft 0 25.0 Oracle 25.8 35.0 US-registered bond deals, $bn, converted at pricing-day rates. Source: Yield Theory from US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, updated 15 November. A broader Reuters and LSEG count puts the five at more than $370bn. 12 Channel Size and date Example Hyperscaler corporate bonds $249.4bn big four, 2026 to 4 Nov 12 Microsoft $25bn on 29 Oct, its first in six years All AI-linked debt $466bn to 1 Nov vs $101bn a year earlier 15 Fed: over $680bn advanced-computing debt by October, 31% of nonfinancial investment-grade issuance 14 Off-balance-sheet vehicles and leases over $1trn unstarted leases plus over $2trn take-or-pay and guarantees 14 Meta Hyperion: maximum exposure $45.95bn 11 Private credit about $800bn of a $1.5trn funding gap, 2025-2028 (Morgan Stanley estimate) 23 17% of 607 Moody's-tracked private borrowers pay interest in kind 24 GPU-backed loans 11 financings, $16.6bn tracked 22 CoreWeave DDTLs at 9-15% effective rates 7 Data centre asset-backed (ABS) and commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) $21.9bn to Nov 2026, 13.1% below 2025 21 $15.3bn asset-backed, $6.6bn mortgage-backed Vendor and circular finance Nvidia guarantees up to $118bn (18 Nov) 20 Oracle uses vendor financing and customer prepayments 17 How the off-balance-sheet chain works Off-balance-sheet SPV financing Bond investors PIMCO and others $27.3bn bonds → Special purpose vehicle Beignet, Blue Owl controlled builds and owns → Data centre campus Hyperion rent plus residual guarantee ↑ Hyperscaler tenant Meta, four-year leases A special purpose vehicle (SPV) borrows against leases from a strong tenant, so the debt sits outside the tenant's accounts. Meta's auditor approved non-consolidation but flagged it as a critical audit matter; Meta discloses maximum exposure of $45.95bn. 11 Nvidia has scaled the idea up: it guarantees the landlord of OpenAI's 4.25GW Ohio campus, with exposure building from fiscal 2029 to a $105bn cap, and OpenAI agreeing to reimburse it. 20 14 The opacity can exacerbate selloffs when investor sentiment shifts, as it is hard to know where risk resides. Fed Governor Michael Barr, citing the Fed's November Financial Stability Report, 16 November 2026 14 Credit markets are already pricing it Oracle five-year CDS spread · bp 0 100 200 300 400 Jun 25: 37.5 Dec 25: 156 Mar 26: 190 Sep 26: 180 20 Oct: 342.5 30 Oct: 293 5 Nov: 305 Jun 25 Dec 25 Mar 26 Sep 26 20 Oct 30 Oct 5 Nov Oracle five-year CDS spread readings Jun 25 37.5 Dec 25 156 Mar 26 190 Sep 26 180 20 Oct 342.5 30 Oct 293 5 Nov 305 Median execution-day spreads, basis points. Source: TradeOnPurpose, 12 November. A bond-implied model put it at 323bp on 20 November; that is modelled, not traded. 16 Oracle (rated BBB- by Standard and Poor's, the lowest investment grade) priced $10bn of notes on 2 November at 240-335bp over Treasuries, coupons 7.00-8.65%. Each 100bp of spread costs it about $1.6bn a year on $155.9bn of debt. 16 17 Meta's new seven-year bonds pay 142bp over Treasuries, double the 68bp earlier in 2026; its order book was $58bn against $125bn a year earlier. New-issue concessions ran 50-60bp. 12 13 CDS on Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle reached their highest since 2021; Alphabet's nearly tripled in a year. Weekly CDS trading on seven AI names topped $9bn in September, as funds use them as a cheap AI hedge. 15 46 CoreWeave was quoted above 1,000bp in early November, with its 2032 bonds near 77 cents on the dollar. Its contract-backed loans still trade near par. 16 8 Banks are pickier: the largest US bank holding companies have close to $1trn of exposure to big tech, developers, AI vehicles, private credit and utilities, per the Fed. 14 25 3. Rates: the squeeze Rate Level Date US 2-year Treasury 4.770% 19 Nov 2026 US 10-year Treasury 5.046% 19 Nov 2026 US 30-year Treasury 5.406% 19 Nov 2026 Fed funds target 3.75-4.00% held 28 Oct 2026 Dec Fed hike priced 94% for 25bp, 6% for 50bp 19 Nov 2026 European Central Bank (ECB) deposit rate 2.50% held 29 Oct 2026 German 10-year Bund about 3.38-3.40% mid-Nov 2026 Sources 26 27 28 . Under Chair Kevin Warsh the Fed is expected to start hiking, with inflation above its 2% target for more than five years. UBS expects 25bp in December and again in March 2027; futures price more than three hikes. Markets also price ECB tightening. 26 28 What higher rates do. A data centre is a long-dated asset with a lease-like income stream, so it is valued like a bond plus growth. Higher long yields raise the discount rate on every future rent, and higher spreads raise the cost of the debt that funds about half of the build. The chip layer is worse: GPUs depreciate over a few years, so their debt has to be repaid fast from rental income whose price is falling. Transaction-based rental indices for H100 chips fell 9.2% in the week to 15 November. 45 Refinancing wall: at least $1trn of data centre debt matures within five years. Developers face $13.4bn of fixed-rate dollar maturities in 2027; refinancing at October Treasury yields would add at least $380m a year (2.85 percentage points). Neocloud maturities bunch in 2030-2032, about $49bn. 25 Moody's flags 2027-2029 as the test for weaker private borrowers. 24 Real estate investment trusts (REITs): Equinix and Digital Realty raised 2026 guidance in Q3 on record bookings, and Digital Realty's cash renewal spreads were up 11.8%. Yet on 22 November Digital Realty's dividend yield was 3.00% and Equinix's 2.08%, about 2.0 and 3.0 percentage points below the 10-year Treasury (our calc). Their valuations rely on growth, which makes them rate-sensitive. 29 30 31 Hyperscalers can absorb it: Microsoft still expects positive free cash flow in fiscal 2027. The squeeze falls on Oracle, neoclouds, developers and the vehicles. 2 4. Where it is headed The November shock had four parts: the midterms (Nasdaq fell 5.56% on 5 November), a Fed that is hiking, the resignation of Nvidia's chief executive on 12 November, and a cool reception for Anthropic's $81bn initial public offering (IPO) on 19 November, when Nvidia fell 14%. More than $1trn came off hyperscaler valuations. Credit access stayed open for the strongest names only. 39 26 20 13 Base case: slower and dearer, not a bust Capex still rises in 2027 but its growth peaks; one broker moved its peak call to 2027 from 2028-2029 after the midterms. 39 Big four keep funding from cash flow plus bonds at wider spreads; more equity and hybrid capital, as Oracle did with $10bn of shares. 13 17 Neoclouds and developers without investment-grade tenants consolidate; contract-backed loans keep flowing at 7-7.5% for the best. 8 Power owners, grid equipment and turbine makers keep pricing power; local politics makes builds slower and dearer rather than stopping them. Bull case: revenue catches up AI revenue and inference demand grow fast enough that free cash flow turns positive on schedule (Oracle targets the second half of fiscal 2028). 18 The Fed stops after one or two hikes and long yields fall back, as UBS argues; spreads narrow, the AI IPO window reopens. 26 Vehicle debt trades like parent debt, confirming the leases are wanted. Bear case: rates plus a revenue miss Hikes continue into 2027 while GPU rental prices fall faster than volumes grow, the telecom 2001 shape. A large AI tenant (an AI lab) fails to fund its commitments, triggering guarantees and leaving campuses half-let. Oracle loses investment grade, forcing index funds to sell, as with Ford and General Motors in 2005. 15 Private credit funds with payment-in-kind (PIK) borrowers and bank lenders take losses; hyperscalers cut capex sharply, hitting suppliers' order books. Our view Base case most likely. The demand signals are still real (Nvidia data centre revenue $107.6bn in its latest quarter, up 110%; Vertiv orders more than doubled), but the financing is now the weak link, and in a 5% world weak links get repriced first. 20 40 Signposts and dates When What Why it matters 8-9 Dec 2026 Fed decision 25bp priced; 50bp would hit leveraged builders hardest December 2026 ECB decision Hike expected; European cost of capital for Nordic builds Coming weeks CoreWeave's investment-grade DDTL Pricing at 7-7.5% would show contract-backed credit still open Late Jan to early Feb 2027 Hyperscaler Q4 results, first 2027 capex numbers Capex against operating cash flow; Meta gives its first 2027 figure First half 2027 Microsoft capex acceleration Confirms or denies the delay story 2027 CoreWeave $10.97bn due; developers $13.4bn due First real refinancing test at 5% yields Spring 2027 Next Fed Financial Stability Report Whether the $3trn off-balance-sheet figure grows End 2027 Nebius pre-tax breakeven target Neocloud model proof point Fiscal 2028-2029 Oracle free cash flow positive, then over $30bn The single biggest credit test in the sector Fiscal 2029 onward Nvidia guarantees go live Vendor support becomes real exposure Ongoing GPU rental indices, Oracle and CoreWeave spreads Earliest warning of a bad boom Sources 8 2 7 25 14 9 18 20 26 . What history adds this time Vendor financing, telecom 2000: Lucent committed $5.7bn of customer credit in 2000; borrower Winstar went bankrupt in April 2001. Nvidia's guarantees are up to $118bn, though most backs one campus with OpenAI as tenant and reimbursing party. 14 20 Rate shocks end booms: the fibre boom broke as the Fed tightened into 2000 and funding shut for the weaker carriers first. The 2026 pattern of strong names borrowing while weaker ones are shut out is the same shape (2026 evidence: 13 ). Shale's borrowing base: banks re-tested shale loans against reserve values twice a year. GPU loans have the same weakness with a faster-ageing asset; watch rental indices as the equivalent of the oil price. Railway politics: local resistance to railways in the 1870s US brought rate regulation. The 2026 ballot results are the first sign that data centres face a political cost of their own. 39 5. Who is exposed Segment Names Our read Chips Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron Strongest cash flows, but now lenders of last resort through guarantees; most sensitive to a capex peak Power and utilities Constellation, Fortum Winners in all but the bear case: scarce power, long contracts (Fortum has a 22-year Google PPA) 44 Gas turbines GE Vernova, Siemens Energy Booked into 2029-2030; data centres under 10% of Siemens Energy backlog, so diversified 33 34 Electrical and cooling Schneider, Vertiv, ABB, Munters Orders strong; most exposed to a sudden capex cut since order books are 12-24 months 40 41 42 Nordic data centre names Munters, Hexatronic, Fortum, NKT Munters most direct (57% of Q3 orders from data centres); Hexatronic 28% of sales 42 43 Data centre REITs Equinix, Digital Realty Good assets, strong leasing; valuation hit by 5% yields Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN Highest risk: floating and high-yield debt against fast-ageing chips Oracle Oracle Equity priced on 2030; credit priced near single-B Lenders Private credit funds, insurers, banks Vehicle and PIK exposure the least visible; banks cushioned per Fed Data gaps No hyperscaler has given a numeric 2027 capex figure; Oracle gives no fiscal 2027 dollar figure. No live traded spread for Meta's Hyperion vehicle bonds is public, so the parent-versus-vehicle gap cannot be tracked. Total private credit lent to data centres is not measured; the Fed says private deals make the total hard to see. Several figures come from secondary aggregators (Yield Theory, TradeOnPurpose, Metacap, GPU index sites) rather than primary filings; Morgan Stanley's gap estimate came via a secondary report with no date. Nordic data centre names' share moves since the November sell-off, Denmark's power price, Nebius total debt and REIT borrowing costs were not found. The Bund yield is an approximate mid-November range; the ECB December meeting date was not checked. The plan of arrangement took effect on 12 November 2026: each NGEx shareholder received one new NGEx share and one fifth of a Valiente share for every NGEx share held.
items.text:
Valiente Resources: company profile at listing (17 Nov 2026)
Listing and shares
Valiente Resources is the Lundin Group exploration company spun out of NGEx Minerals to hold the Valle Ancho copper-gold project. The plan of arrangement took effect on 12 November 2026: each NGEx shareholder received one new NGEx share and one fifth of a Valiente share for every NGEx share held.
43,371,756 Valiente shares were issued and outstanding at completion. NGEx options were exchanged for fully vested Valiente options over one fifth of a share each; the circular put these at options over about 2.24 million Valiente shares.
The shares are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange as a Tier 2 mining issuer under the ticker VALX and first traded on 16 November 2026. There is no Stockholm or other European line. Market value at the first close was about C$152 million (shares at completion times the first-day close).
Financial year end is 31 August (TSX Venture company summary). Auditor PricewaterhouseCoopers; transfer agent Computershare.
Valle Ancho project
Valle Ancho is 100% owned and straddles the Argentina-Chile border. The Argentine claims lie in Catamarca Province, 56 to 140 km west of the town of Fiambalá, held through Pampa Catamarca S.A.; the Chilean claims lie in Region III. The project sits immediately east of the Maricunga Gold Belt (Cerro Casale, Caspiche, La Coipa).
Argentina: 33 granted and eight pending permits (cateos) over 105,609 hectares. All targets so far are on the Argentine side, on the Nordin 1, Nordin 4, La Quebrada 1, La Quebrada 2, La Austral 1 and Interceptor 6 claims.
Chile: 15 granted exploitation concessions and 33 granted exploration concessions, 12,650 hectares gross or 8,610 hectares net of overlaps. No exploration work has been done on the Chilean claims.
The project has two areas. The Valle Ancho area covers the Nordin and La Quebrada targets; the Interceptor area covers the Interceptor porphyry and the Los Aparejos skarn. By style: porphyry copper-gold at La Quebrada and Interceptor, Maricunga-style porphyry gold at Nordin, epithermal gold-silver at La Austral, and copper-gold skarn at Los Aparejos.
NGEx drilled a 3,060 m scout programme in 2022. Selected results from the company presentation: La Quebrada hole VADH003 cut 596 m of 0.50% copper equivalent (0.23% copper, 0.37 g/t gold, 1.4 g/t silver) and VADH006 cut 423 m of 0.40% copper equivalent; at Nordin, VAD001 cut 150 m of 1.05 g/t gold and VAD002 198 m of 0.63 g/t gold. The company says it has several drill-ready targets. A technical report by SLR dated 6 Nov 2026 is on its website.
Valiente is an exploration-stage company with no mineral resource. Catamarca charges a sliding-scale copper and gold royalty of 2% to 5%, and some Chilean claims carry a 1.5% net smelter return royalty to a previous owner.
Funding and first-year plan
Before completion NGEx contributed about C$16.6 million. This paid for the Chilean concessions and the shares of Pampa Catamarca S.A., and left about C$2.0 million of working capital.
The 12-month budget in the circular is C$2.0 million: Phase 1 work programme C$625,800 (prospecting, surface sampling, more geophysics and core storage), Argentine property costs C$577,425, other property costs C$245,219, general and administrative costs C$399,312 and C$152,244 unallocated. The company says it will raise more money when it needs it.
Strategy
Besides Valle Ancho, Valiente plans to build a portfolio of copper, gold and silver exploration assets through selective acquisitions, starting in Argentina and Chile. Head office is Suite 2800, 1055 Dunsmuir Street, Vancouver, shared with NGEx.
Board and management
Wojtek Wodzicki is Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer, the same roles he holds at NGEx. Alex Tong is Chief Financial Officer and Heidi Chik is Corporate Secretary. The other directors are Robert Carmichael, Joyce Ngo and Nathan Monash.
Ownership
Nemesia S.à r.l., a company controlled by a trust settled by the late Adolf H. Lundin, held 73,671,714 NGEx shares (33.97%) at the record date. Valiente shares went out pro rata, so this implies about 14.7 million Valiente shares, or about 34%. No Valiente filing has confirmed the figure yet.
NGEx directors and officers as a group were expected to hold about 1.35 million Valiente shares (about 3.12%) plus options over 1.625 million shares.

items.text:
Orinduik: Navitas option and the Guyana licence (12 Nov 2026)
Where things stand
The Eco–Navitas framework was signed in early December 2025. Navitas paid US$2m for options over Orinduik and Block 1 CBK, the Orange Basin block off South Africa. The Orinduik option is exercisable within 12 months for US$2.5m and gives Navitas 80% and operatorship, carrying Eco's 20% up to US$11m net, excluding mobilisation.
The Block 1 CBK farm-down completed on 22 September 2026. Navitas took 37.5% and operatorship, paid US$4m in cash, and will carry Eco for up to US$7.5m net.
The Orinduik licence expired on 14 January 2026 at the end of its second renewal. Eco says the Petroleum Act keeps its rights to the Jethro-1 and Joe-1 discoveries (2019, heavy oil) while its appraisal programme is reviewed.
On 22 May 2026 the minister, Vickram Bharrat, said no extension was granted for Orinduik or Canje. Canje expired on 4 March 2026; Eco has an indirect interest in Canje through JHI Associates. Both blocks must apply for new licences under the new production sharing agreement (PSA).
Eco had guided a new PSA by September, in the third quarter. On 1 October the minister confirmed that none had been issued. Eco says talks are progressing well. Nothing newer was found as of 12 November 2026.
Why it is slow
This section is an analyst read, not a reason given by the government. The government has given no stated reason for this delay.
Guyana has been deliberately tougher on terms after criticism of the Exxon Stabroek deal. The old Orinduik terms were a 1% royalty, a 75% cost-recovery cap, and no corporate income tax, with the state paying the company's tax from its profit oil. The new PSA has a 10% royalty, a 10% corporate tax and a 65% cost-recovery cap. Moving onto the new terms means a renegotiation, not a rollover, and makes the economics of appraising heavy oil harder.
Other factors also point the same way: a small energy ministry stretched by Exxon's new projects, the 2022 licensing round and the gas-to-shore project; caution after the 2025 election about signing anything that looks like a giveaway; and caution offshore given Venezuela's claim over the Essequibo region.
Any falling-out?
There is no sign of a falling-out. Neither side has publicly criticised the other, and Eco has described the talks as constructive and progressing well. The same treatment was applied to the Canje block, so Eco has not been singled out.
The only point of tension is Eco's view that it keeps its rights to the two discoveries, against the ministry's line that the licence "has come to an end". Neither side has escalated it.
Likely path
The figures below are the author's judgement, not figures from any source.
About 50–60%: the December option deadline is extended, or the terms are amended, tied to the licence award. This is the most likely path.
About 25–30%: Guyana issues the new PSA before December and Navitas exercises close to the original terms.
About 15–20%: the option lapses, Eco keeps Orinduik and looks for another partner or a sole-risk path.
The reason is that Navitas is unlikely to pay US$2.5m and take on a carry of up to US$11m before it knows the new fiscal terms. Both sides still want the deal, as shown by the Block 1 CBK completion.
Things to watch: any Guyana statement on the Orinduik PSA, and Eco's December update around the option deadline.
